unit.why: A single anecdote about R. Naftali of Ropshitz in his youth exposing the pride of an ascetic townsman through a staged rebuke.
unit.boundary_note: division ends with a garbled running head/catchword ('איש אתלי זצ"ל אבד״ק ראפשיץ הה"ק ר׳ נא') that is not part of the story

stories.start_quote: הה"ק ר׳ נפתלי זצ״ל אבד״ק ראפשיץ
stories.summary_en: In his youth R. Naftali of Ropshitz sensed that a much-fasting townsman had grown proud, so he pushed a boy into him and loudly scolded the boy, praising the man for fasting on Mondays and Thursdays. The man replied in Yiddish that it was not 'from Sabbath to Sabbath', which exposed his pride, and onlookers grasped the rabbi's wisdom.
